summary: Feed s132_double to NDR is degraded: 98.5% encrypted traffic exceeds 90% tolerance and VLAN 20 is missing (50% untagged), severely limiting payload inspection and segmentation visibility.

findings.root_cause: 98.5% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) forwarded without broker-side decryption or selective handling, exceeding the NDR's 90% encrypted tolerance. Indicates broker is mirroring predominantly encrypted flows as-is.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for deep inspection and behavioral detection; with almost all payload opaque, detection coverage collapses and threats inside encrypted sessions are missed.

recommended_fix.why: NDR cannot analyze encrypted payloads - provide cleartext via compliant decryption (with key escrow/privacy controls) or filter/route so inspectable traffic is within tolerance

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 never observed and 50% of packets are untagged, indicating packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags or ingress/egress ports are not configured as trunks to preserve VLANs 10 and 20.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR loses tenant/segment context for VLAN 20 and half the traffic; VLAN-aware policies, attribution, and detection for that segment fail, creating a blind spot.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags through the broker so NDR receives correctly tagged traffic for both required VLANs and can apply segment-aware detection
